teams.heading: Fiji record 63-10 win over Canada as highest score in 11 tests
teams.body: Fiji’s 63-10 victory against Canada in September 2025 remains the side's largest winning margin across their last 11 matches. During this window, which includes the Pacific Nations Cup knockout stage, the Flying Fijians have maintained a scoring average of 28.5 points per game. However, the team has conceded an average of 31.9 points per fixture. In total, Fiji have scored 314 points and shipped 351 throughout this 11-game sequence of international tests.

teams.heading: Benhard Janse van Rensburg stretchered off after Bristol Bears victory
teams.body: England centre Benhard Janse van Rensburg was stretchered off in a distressing scene during Saturday's Premiership clash at Ashton Gate. The Bristol midfielder required an eight-minute stoppage for treatment after colliding with Northampton’s Henry Pollock in the first half. While his teammates secured a 41-26 win, the incident overshadowed the result, with the player knocked out in the collision. Elsewhere, Will Joseph’s performance in Gloucester's 48-0 win over Harlequins has prompted further calls for his inclusion in the international setup.

teams.heading: Peter O’Mahony explains how Rassie Erasmus’ departure impacted him at Munster
teams.body: Former Munster captain Peter O’Mahony has shared the personal toll of Rassie Erasmus’ sudden departure from the club in 2017. Reflecting on their time working together, O’Mahony admitted he was hurt when Erasmus exited to lead the Springboks, stating, “I was hurt because I trusted him and I was all into his game plan.” While acknowledging the move as a professional necessity, the flanker noted that the team felt a tangible loss of direction following the coach’s exit.

teams.heading: Italy men’s XV reflect on previous world ranking peaks
teams.body: The Italy men's side has reached a highest-ever world ranking of No. 8 on two separate occasions. This peak was first achieved in 2007, and the national team most recently equalled that position in 2024. These historical markers remain the highest points the team has attained in the official World Rugby rankings.

teams.heading: Bath monitoring Edinburgh scrum-half Hector Patterson amid potential England eligibility
teams.body: Bath are reportedly tracking Edinburgh scrum-half Hector Patterson as the 21-year-old nears the end of his current contract. While Patterson has represented Scotland through the age-grade system, including a World Rugby U20 Trophy title in 2024, he remains eligible for England via a grandparent. Although currently committed to Edinburgh, the prospect of a move to the Premiership has raised questions about his long-term international allegiance with the 2027 World Cup cycle approaching.

teams.heading: Dragons defeat Scarlets in high-scoring encounter at Rodney Parade
teams.body: The Dragons secured a 36-26 victory over the Scarlets in a competitive United Rugby Championship derby on Saturday. The home side capitalised on their opportunities to cross the whitewash six times, including a brace from hooker Elliot Dee. Despite a strong start from the visitors, who led at the interval, the Dragons regained control in the second half. The result marks a significant result for the Dragons following a hard-fought contest that saw the Scarlets reduced to 14 men late on.

teams.body: As the senior men’s side prepares for the upcoming international schedule, the team continues to look back at their historical benchmarks. Following their recent results in the current international season, including the loss to England, the squad remains focused on climbing back toward that level as they look ahead to their next fixture against Ireland.

teams.heading: Japan Sakura XV women suffer seven-try defeat against Ireland in Cork
teams.body: The Japan Sakura XV women's side concluded their recent tour with a 43-19 loss to Ireland in Cork on Saturday. Despite an early try from Sakurako Korai, the visitors were unable to contain the hosts' physical set-piece, conceding seven tries in total. This result follows the Sakura XV’s 31-24 defeat in the WXV Global Series match held in Galway the previous weekend, marking consecutive losses against the Irish side as they continue their preparations for future international competition.

teams.heading: Zoe Harrison secures dramatic Red Roses victory over New Zealand women's team
teams.body: The England women's team extended their unbeaten run to 41 tests after Zoe Harrison scored a decisive interception try in overtime to defeat New Zealand 26-19 at the Allianz Stadium. The Black Ferns held a half-time lead following a resilient attacking display, which included a first-half try from centre Amy Du Plessis. However, discipline proved costly for the visitors in the second 40 minutes, culminating in a yellow card for Veisinia Mahutariki-Fakalelu as the Red Roses fought back to claim the WXV fixture.
